findings.finding: F1: moving session resolution off GET /v1/sessions breaks roughly 50 Go stub listeners that serve only that path, three read-count assertions (comment_delivery_resolution_test.go:100-104, :345, :399) and the WaitGroup barrier armed for exactly two list reads (broadcast_idempotency_test.go:223-227).
findings.answer: Tasks T3, T4 and T5 each name the stub listeners they extend with the new route and require the counting assertions to count per-session reads; T4 re-arms the idempotency barrier on the per-session route, where one broadcast of one session makes exactly one read.

findings.finding: F2: the browser harness's fake listener answers any unknown path with a plain-text 404, which Dispatch's client reads as ErrUnavailable, so a new listener route silently breaks every delivery spec.
findings.answer: D12 and T6.1 add the route to packages/dispatch/e2e/fake-envoy.ts, with three record states, and T6.6 lists the send-refusal specs that must keep working untouched.

findings.finding: F3: the broadcast composer computes its recipients from the same cache-backed agents list, so a person cannot select a session the list has already dropped, and acceptance 2 is invisible through the page under that reading.
findings.answer: D11 keeps every list a cache view and says why; the plan proves acceptance 2 for the case a person can reach (sessions the page listed that leave the list before the send arrives, T6.3), and the composer's limit is reported to the architect rather than built.

findings.finding: F4: none of the surfaces the spec names can host the acceptance tests as written, and no criterion named a command.
findings.answer: The acceptance table gives every criterion a surface, an exact command and a negative control; T8 builds the cross-service Go proof (real listener mux, real Dispatch mux, real NATS, real Postgres through internal/testpg, which never skips) and adds its Postgres image to the envoy-go pre-pull step; departure 1 records the proof's home.

findings.finding: F5: acceptance 4 lives in the Dispatch client's error classification, and the per-id precedent (Role) returns an error that is neither ErrNotFound nor ErrUnavailable, so a 503 would reach createBroadcast unclassified and answer 500.
findings.answer: D5 and T2 define Session's mapping: 404, 400 and 413 are ErrNotFound; every other status, decode failure and transport failure is ErrUnavailable, tested status by status.

findings.finding: F6: which route serves the per-session read, what body it returns, and the fate of /v1/registry/<id> were open, and that route's raw body carries no session_id and an empty host.
findings.answer: D1 extends GET /v1/registry/<session_id>; D2 makes its body the same object a row of GET /v1/sessions carries, built by one shared helper (T1.3); D11 states that GET /v1/sessions itself is unchanged.

findings.finding: F7: a broadcast whose per-session read did not answer could fail whole or partially, and the idempotency key would freeze a partial answer for that key.
findings.answer: D7 refuses the whole send with 503 ENVOY_UNAVAILABLE and writes nothing, as today's unreadable list does, so no transient failure becomes a stored exclusion; T4 and acceptance A4 assert it.

findings.finding: F8: the refusal wording is load-bearing in three forms, and the temporary text must not collide with the prefix comment_delivery.go:53 classifies on.
findings.answer: D6 keeps both absence texts byte-identical and routes the temporary one through deliveryErrorText; T3 and A4 require a test that the temporary text never begins with 'no live session '.

findings.finding: F9: up to 100 per-session reads inside one synchronous broadcast request, against a 2 s listener read and a 10 s JetStream wait, is up to 200 s serial.
findings.answer: D8 bounds it: at most 8 concurrent reads under one 5 s budget taken from the request context, and a budget that ends refuses as D7 says; D9 records that the mention path's call count is unchanged.

findings.finding: F10: acceptance 1 says 'is delivered', but the listener's send route still reads the cache alone and that fix belongs to the unmerged dispatch://INFRA-141.
findings.answer: The first risk records it: the delivery succeeds because the authoritative read writes what it read into the cache (registry.go:341), the cross-service proof asserts the delivery end to end, and the limit (more than one listener behind ENVOY_URL, or a cache emptied again between the two calls) is written down rather than assumed.

findings.finding: F11: the issue-claim takeover asks the same per-id question through the same list, and 'not listed' means 'free to take', so a working session's claim can be taken while the cache refills.
findings.answer: D10 fixes it in this issue (T5), with its own acceptance line A5, and departure 2 records the added scope for the architect.

findings.finding: F12: the issue list's route_status reads the same list, must stay list-based, and already owns the gone-versus-did-not-answer vocabulary.
findings.answer: D11 states that route_status, the agents page and the subscribers page are unchanged and why, and matches this plan's refusals to their existing no_holder/unknown vocabulary.

findings.finding: F13: four claims the plan would lean on are unverified here (INFRA-141's helper as merged code, the client-go citation, the incident's listing symptom), and the closest in-repo precedent (adminInterestsHandler's 404-versus-503 rule) was uncited.
findings.answer: The plan cites adminInterestsHandler (api.go:731-741) and store.Registry.Get (internal/store/kv.go:701-721) as the in-repo rules, links the client-go documentation, records in D3, D4 and the risks that INFRA-141's constant and helper do not exist on this base, and says in 'Reported to the architect' that the listing symptom is not closed here.

findings.finding: F14: a session id NATS refuses as a key would answer 404 through Refresh's mapping, while the listener's own convention for such an id is 400.
findings.answer: D3 and T1.2 check bus.ErrRefused first and answer through writeNATSError (400 or 413), with rows added to the key-refusal table test; D5 maps 400 and 413 to ErrNotFound on the Dispatch side, as Interest already does.

specDepartures.spec: Acceptance 1 names the proof surface as 'a Go test in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch against a NATS container', beside packages/envoy/scripts/e2e-local.sh.
specDepartures.plan: The cross-service proof lives in packages/envoy/cmd/listener (T8) and imports the Dispatch server, rather than living in internal/dispatch and importing the listener; scripts/e2e-local.sh additionally checks the new route against the real listener binary (T7).
specDepartures.evidence: The listener's HTTP mux is built by registerV1Routes in package main (packages/envoy/cmd/listener/api.go:1069), so no package outside cmd/listener can construct it, and the only deterministic cold-cache rigs are that package's own (api_test.go:805-828 trailingListeners, :955-966 stallSessionReads). api.Register and api.NewDeps are exported (internal/dispatch/api/server.go:303, :157) and internal/testpg.URL needs no TestMain, so the Dispatch server can be built from there.

acceptance: Acceptance 1's parenthetical surface: the Go test is in packages/envoy/cmd/listener rather than packages/envoy/internal/dispatch; what it proves (both services real, against a NATS container, with the cache cold) is unchanged.

specDepartures.spec: The spec's Acceptance names a comment mention and a broadcast, and its 'Not this issue' section excludes only dispatch://INFRA-141 and dispatch://INFRA-246.
specDepartures.plan: The plan also fixes the issue-claim takeover, where Dispatch asks whether a claim holder is still working by scanning the same live-session list, and adds acceptance line A5 for it (D10, T5).
specDepartures.evidence: packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/issue_claim.go:138-156 fetches the whole list to judge one holder, and claimBlockedBy at :209-213 reads 'not listed' as 'the claim is free to take', so during a refill a working session's issue claim is taken with no force flag; the same file's comment at :134-136 already forbids 'unknown, therefore free'. This deployment's instructions forbid deferring an adjacent defect.

outcome.scope: One more call site is fixed (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/issue_claim.go) and one acceptance line is added (A5: a working session's issue claim is not taken while the cache refills).
acceptance: Added A5: with the listener's session cache refilling and the holder's record in the store, another caller's claim of the issue is refused with the holder's conflict, where today it is granted.
